lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! Let me help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit. I'll need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First, let me ask about your child's age:**

How old is your child? This will help me determine which eligibility path to follow:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old  
- 20 years old or over

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is between 16-19 years old, I need to check additional criteria. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now for Alex who is 17, I need to know about his education or training status:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (currently enrolled and studying), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR  
3. **Neither** of the above (not in education/training and left more than 20 weeks ago)

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is currently in education studying for his A-levels at sixth form. Let me check the education level requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are an approved qualification for Child Benefit. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**Questions about Alex's A-level course:**

1. **Is it full-time?** (Does it involve at least 12 hours per week of supervised study?)

2. **Is it funded by an employer** or linked to an agreement for a future job with an employer?

3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (This only matters if he is, and if so, whether he's financially dependent on you)

Please let me know about these details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's full-time - he's there during the week like a normal school schedule. No, it's not funded by any employer - it's just regular sixth form. And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

Excellent! Alex's A-level course meets the requirements. Now I need to check about his work status:

**Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week?** (Or is he not in paid work at all?)

For young people aged 16+, if they work 24 hours or more per week, they wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does have a part-time job at the supermarket. Actually, now that you mention it, he works quite a bit - it's more or less full-time hours there, so yeah, it would be 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see. Thank you for being honest about that. Since Alex is working 24 hours or more per week, let me navigate to the outcome for this situation.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment - Result

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

While Alex is doing well by studying for his A-levels at sixth form (which is normally an approved qualification), the issue is that **he is working 24 or more hours per week** at his supermarket job. 

Under UK Child Benefit rules, a young person aged 16 or over who works 24+ hours per week does not qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes, even if they are also in approved education.

### What you can do:

**If Alex's work hours reduce:** If Alex reduces his working hours to less than 24 hours per week while continuing his A-level studies, he would become eligible again, and you could claim Child Benefit at that point.

**If he returns to full-time education only:** If Alex stops working (or significantly reduces his hours) to focus on his studies, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again.

I understand this might be disappointing news, especially since Alex is working hard both at his studies and his job. If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to ask or contact HMRC's Child Benefit office for further guidance.
